notes: Two artifacts a real run wrote, both over the 1-5 line bound: eight non-blank TL;DR lines in the target-state plan and six in the clarifications. The sibling tldr-six-lines already pins the lint and is hand-built, which proves the check fires on a document someone typed; these are the bytes of a writer that was following its instructions, and nothing in those instructions mentions a length. The orchestrators' Artifact Summary Contract requires the block and its four headings; the bound lives in the register, which no subagent reads. Two of that run's three artifacts breached it, so the rule holds today where a writer happens to be terse rather than because anything holds it there. Both files are absent from valid/runs/migration-cjs-to-esm for this reason and live here instead of being reworded, because rewording sampled prose to fit a rule is how the breach stops being visible. Truncated after their summary block, like every artifact sampled from that run. Delete this fixture with the bound if the bound goes; keep it if the length moves into the writers, where it becomes the case that proves they were told.
